disposition_reason: Greenhouse pot trial of four biochars at 1% and 2% w/w in two Ecuadorian cacao-farm soils (natural and Cd-spiked) with CCN-51 rooted cuttings for 130 days. Outcomes are extractable soil Cd and leaf/stem/root Cd of young plants; no beans or cocoa products were analysed, so there are no occurrence findings and the results are pot-scale mitigation evidence for a leaf proxy.
disposition_locator: Abstract; Sections 2.1-2.5 (PDF pp.2-3); Table 2 (PDF p.6); Tables S4, S6

study.design: pot trial (greenhouse, completely randomized, 3 replicates, 108 units)
study.material_scope: cacao soil and leaves/stems/roots of 6-month-old CCN-51 rooted cuttings; no beans
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Soils from two cacao farms in Ecuador: Manabí (slightly alkaline, pH 7.30) and Azuay (moderately acidic, pH 5.52); plants grown in greenhouse (location not stated beyond Ecuadorian institutions)
study.sampling_unit: pot (4 kg soil, one plant); n=3 per soil x Cd x treatment cell
study.method: Plant tissue: HNO3 digestion 80 °C 6 h, ICP-OES; soil pseudo-total Cd: aqua regia, ICP-OES; extractable Cd: 0.01 M CaCl2, 1 M NH4OAc, 0.1 M HCl
study.lod_loq: ICP-OES Cd LOD 8 µg/L (solution basis; supplement S1)
study.basis: plant tissue dried 65 °C, dry weight; soil air-dried
study.qa: CRMs NIST 2709a (soil) and NIST 1573a (plant); recoveries 103 ± 1.60% soil, 97 ± 2.00% plant; blanks/duplicates every 20 samples (supplement Description S1)

controls.control: Soil biochar amendment: coffee-husk biochar (550 °C) at 1% w/w (dry soil), CCN-51 rooted-cutting plants, 130 days
controls.comparator: unamended control soil, same soil (slightly alkaline, non-spiked); n=3 per treatment, mean ± SE
controls.outcome: leaf Cd 2.9±0.4 a -> 3.1±0.4 a mg/kg (+7%; source Tukey letters shown); leaf-Cd reduction factor (control/treated) 1.0±0.1 b (Table S6); CaCl2-extractable soil Cd below ICP-OES detection in this soil (not reported); NH4OAc-extractable soil Cd 98.3±3.3 -> 85.0±2.9 µg/kg (-14%); HCl-extractable soil Cd 471±17 -> 446±20 µg/kg. Plant tissue is leaves of young plants (6 months old at transplant, harvested after 130 days; no beans produced); leaf Cd dry weight. Percent changes calculated from Table 2 means.

context_notes: Soil pseudo-total Cd: slightly alkaline 0.57 (SD 0.06) mg/kg, moderately acidic 0.61 (0.12) mg/kg; after spiking with 1.00 mg Cd/kg: 1.38 (0.44) and 1.64 (0.14) mg/kg (Section 2.3).
Authors state bean Cd at both source farms exceeded 0.60 mg/kg (citing Argüello et al. 2019); no bean values are given in this paper.

Introduction cites secondary bean-Cd averages (Ecuador 0.9, Peru 1.0, Honduras 2.5, Colombia 4.0, Africa 0.3 mg/kg) from other studies; these are not this paper's data and are not extracted as findings.
Stem and root Cd (Table S4) follow leaf trends: e.g. Quinoa-BC2% stem Cd 3.6 -> 2.0 mg/kg (alkaline non-spiked) and 13.7 -> 8.0 mg/kg (acidic spiked); root Cd not significantly changed.
Quinoa-BC 2% is stated as equivalent to about 40 t/ha (40 Mg/ha) in the field.
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary's 'up to 48%' leaf-Cd reduction is the abstract figure; Table 2 means give Quinoa-BC2% leaf-Cd changes of -38% (alkaline non-spiked, not significant), -15% (alkaline spiked), -43% (acidic non-spiked) and -54% (acidic spiked). The summary does not note that the plant tissue is leaves of young plants, not beans, beyond calling it leaf Cd.

Stored summary says bean Cd at both farms exceeded the 0.60 mg/kg 'trading threshold used for EU chocolate-market access'; the paper calls 0.60 mg/kg both 'the European Union limit for Cd in chocolate' (Section 2.1) and an 'unofficial industry threshold' for beans (Introduction).
integrity_issues: Section 3.3 states average leaf Rf for Quinoa-BC2% of 2.01 in non-spiked slightly alkaline soil, but Table S6 gives 1.7 ± 0.3 and the Table 2 means give 2.9/1.8 = 1.6.

Section 3.3 says Quinoa-BC2% significantly lowered leaf Cd in Cd-spiked slightly alkaline soil, but Table 2 Tukey letters (control ab, Quinoa-BC2% b) do not separate them; only the Rf in Table S6 (1.2 a) differs.
Abstract '~48%' leaf-Cd reduction cannot be reproduced from Table 2 (computed -15% to -54%, mean about -38%).
Table 2 prints the acidic spiked control leaf Cd as '13,9' (decimal comma).
Discussion says leaf Cd was 1.8- and 2.5-fold lower with Quinoa-BC2% in alkaline and acidic soils and later gives average Rf 1.6 and 2.0; these averages differ from each other and from Table S6.
unresolved: No cacao bean or cocoa product measurements: the leaf-to-bean extrapolation rests on correlations from other studies (r = 0.74 and 0.91 cited); bean-level mitigation magnitude is not established by this trial.
Collection date of soils and greenhouse period are not reported.
